OBITUARY REFERENCES AND REFERENCE REGARDING 
MASSACRE AT KASIM NAGAR IN JAMMU 
MR. CHAIRMAN: Hon. Members, it is with deep sorrow that I refer 
to the passing away of Shri Basappa Danappa Jatti, former Chairman of the 
Rajya Sabha, on the 7th June, 2002, at Bangalore, at the age of 90. 
Born at Savalgi village, Jamkhandi Taluka, Bijapur District, 
Karnataka, on September 10, 1912, Shri Jatti had his education at 
Government High School, Bijapur, and Rajaram College and Sykes Law 
College, Kolhapur. 
Shri Jatti started his career as a lawyer in Jamkhandi. He was 
actively involved in social welfare activities, village development projects and 
literary institutions. He participated in the liberation movement of the 
princely State of Jamkhandi. 
The political career of Shri Jatti began when he became a Member of 
the Legislature in the prin cely State of Jamkhandi. He served as a Minister 
under the Maharaja of that State, and later became the Chief Minister. During 
his tenure as Chief Minister, Shri Jatti piloted a proposal for merger of the 
princely State of Jamkhandi with the Indian Union. He was the first to do so 
in South India. After the merger, Shri Jatti was nominated as a Member of the 
Legislative Assembly of the then composite State of Bombay, and was 
appointed as the Parliame ntary Secretary to the th en Chief Minister of 
Bombay. He also served as the Deputy  Minister of Health and Labour, and 
later held the charge as Minister of Health and Labour. 
Consequent upon the reorganisation of States in 1956, Shri Jatti 
became a Member of the Legislative Assembly of Mysore State. He was 
appointed as the Chairman of the La nd Reforms Committee. This Committee 
submitted a report which was later known as "Jatti Committee 
1 

RAJYA SABHA [15 July, 2002] 
Report" and it dealt with all the problems as well as possible solutions in 
regard to land reforms in the State. 
Shri Jatti served as the Chief Minister of Mysore State from 1958 to 
1962. He also served as the Finance Minister of the State in 1962 and 
Minister of Food in 1966.   He was re-elected to the Assembly in 1967. 
Prior to his elevation as the Vice-Pr esident of India in August, 1974, 
Shri Jatti was Lt. Governor of Pondicherry from 1968 to T972. He was 
appointed Governor of Orissa in November, 1972. As. Chairman of the Rajya 
Sabha from 1974 to 1979, Shri Jatti conducted the proceedings of the House 
with wisdom, vision and insight. He made a rich contribution to the high 
traditions established by his distingu ished predecessors, by his objectivity, 
impartiality, understanding and meticulous devotion to all matters concerning 
Rajya Sabha. These qualities helped him to harmonize the conflciting 
viewpoints in the House and conduct the proceedings in a fair and dignified 
manner. 
Shri Jatti also authored a number of articles on philosophy and 
literature. 
In the passing away of Shri Jatti, the country has lost an able 
administrator and an eminent social worker. 
Hon. Members, I also refer with profound sorrow to the passing 
away of Shri Chandra Mohan Sinha, Shri Gulsher Ahmed and Shri Sundar 
Mohun Hemrom, former Members, Shri Mukesh R. Patel, a sitting Member, 
Shri Jagdambi Prasad Yadav and Shri Mohd. Masud Khan, former Members 
of this House. 
Shri Chandra Mohan Sinha passed away on the 13 th May, 2002, at 
Bhubaneshwar at the age of 79. 
Born at Durgapur village in Mayurbhanj district of Orissa in March, 
1923, Shri Sinha had his education at Government High School and 
Ravenshaw College, Cuttack. An active political and social worker, Shri 
Sinha worked for the uplift of the tribal people and development of tribal 
areas. He was in Government service from 1943 to 1949 and then resigned to 
work for the cause of the downtrodde n people. He was associated with 
Prajamandal Movement and Adibasi Congress in Orissa. He was also General 
Secretary of several trade unions. Shri Sinha established many schools and 
colleges and took up many development projects in tribal areas with public 
cooperation. 
2 

[15 July, 2002] RAJYA SABHA 
The legislative career of Shri Sinh a started with the membership of 
the Orissa Legislative Assembly during 1961 to 1967. Shri Sinha served as 
the Deputy Minister in the Orissa Government, holding portfolios of Labour, 
Home, Revenue and Excise, between 1962 and 1967. Shri Sinha was also a 
Member of the Fifth and Sixth Lok Sabhas. 
Shri Sinha represented the State of Orissa in this House from March 
1991 to July 1992. 
In the passing away of Shri Sinha, the country has lost a veteran 
parliamentarian, devoted  social worker and a trade unionist. 
Shri Gulsher Ahmed passed away on the 20th May, 2002, at Satna, at 
the age of 81. 
Born at Satna, in August, 1921, Shri Ahmed had his education at 
Satna, Allahabad, and University Colle ge, London, and was called to the Bar 
from the Inner Temple. 
A lawyer by vocation, Shri Ahmed started his legislative career as a 
Member of this House and represented the State of Madhya Pradesh 
(erstwhile Vindhya Pradesh) in this House from April, 1952 to April 1956. 
Shri Ahmed served as the Deputy  Minister and Minister in the 
Madhya Pradesh Government, holding portfolios of Law and Finance, Law 
and Revenue, between 1962 and 1967. He was the Speaker of the Madhya 
Pradesh Legislative Assembly from 1972 to 1977. 
Shri Ahmed was elected to the Seventh Lok Sabha and was 
Chairman of the Committee on Offices of Profit in the Lok Sabha. 
Shri Ahmed served as the Governor of Himachal Pradesh from June 
to November, 1993. He was appointed as Chancellor of the Mahatma Gandhi 
Gramodaya Vishva-Vidhyalaya from June to July, 1997. 
In the passing away of Shri Gulsher Ahmed, the country has lost an 
able administrator and a veteran parliamentarian. 
Shri Sundar Mohun Hemrom passed away on the 26 th May, 2002 at 
Tarana at the age of 83, after a prolonged illness. 
Born at Tarana, in October, 1919, Shri Hemrom had his education at 
Baripada H.E. School and Ravenshaw College, Cuttack. 
A homoeopath medical practitioner by vocation, Shri Hemrom was 
3 

RAJYA SABHA [15 July, 2002] 
associated with various socio-economic and cultural organisations of the 
Adivasis. He was also organizer and advisor to the Mayurbhanj Adibasi 
Sabha. Shri Hemrom was editor of th e "Sagen Sakam" a fortnightly in 
Santhali language from 1947 to 1949. 
Shri Hemrom represented the State of Orissa in this House from 
April, 1952 to April, 1956. 
In the passing away of Shri Hemr om, the country has lost a noted 
social worker who championed the cause of Adivasis. 
Shri Mukesh R. Patel passed away on the 15 th June, 2002, at 
Mumbai, at the age of 48, following card iac arrest. Born at Nadiad (Gujarat) 
in September, 1954, Shri Patel had his education at Maharajwada Uchattar 
Madhyamik Vidyalaya. A businessman by profession, Shri Patel was 
associated with various social welfar e and cultural organisations and made 
valuable contributions to enrich public life, in various capacities. He took keen 
interest, specially, in the field of economic and financial matters. Shri Patel 
represented the State of Maharashtra in  this House for two consecutive terms 
from February, 1996 to April, 2002, and again, from April, 2002, till his death. 
In the passing away of Shri Mukesh R. Patel, the country has lost an 
entrepreneur and an active parliamentarian. 
Shri Jagdambi Prasad Yadav passed away on the 20 th June, 2002, at 
Coimbatore at the age of 78. Born at village Ekashitola, District Monghyr 
(Bihar) in January, 1925. Shri Yadav had his education at.Monghyr, Patna, 
Bhagalpur and Varanasi. An advocate by profession, Shri Yadav was an active 
political and social worker. He worked for the welfare of the Harijans and set 
up a library and contributed towards propagation of education. He participated 
actively in the freedom struggle from 1942 to 1946. He also participated in the 
movement started by Lok Nayak Jai Prakash Narayan, and was imprisoned 
several times in 1949. He was engaged in preservation and development of 
Indian culture and heritage. He worked as Chairman and Director in the field 
of cooperatives. He was President of the Bhartiya Jana Sangh, Bihar State, 
from 1968 to 1971, and President of the Bhartiya Janata Party, Bihar State, 
from 1981 to 1984. 
The distinguished legislative career of Shri Yadav started with the 
membership of the Bihar Legislative Assembly from 1962, and continued till 
1967. He was a Member of the Sixth, Eleventh, Twelfth and the Thirteenth 
4 

[15 July, 2002]                      RAJYA SABHA 
Lok Sabhas. He represented the State of Bihar in this House for two terms 
from April 1968 to April 1974, and again, from April 1982 to April 1988. He 
also served as the Union Minister of State in the Ministries of Health and 
Family Welfare and Industry from 1977 to 1979, and again, from 1981 to 
1984. Shri Yadav visited many countries in different capacities and 
represented India at several international events. 
In the passing away of Shri Jagdambi Prasad Yadav, the country has 
lost an eminent parliamentarian and a social worker. 
Shri Mohd. Masud Khan passed away on 3rd July, 2002, at the age of 
74, following a tragic car accident in  Delhi. Born at village Monari, 
Azamgarh, Uttar Pradesh, Shri Khan had his education at Allahabad and 
Azamgarh. An advocate and agriculturi st by vocation, Shri Khan was 
associated with various educational and social welfare organisations in 
different capacities. Shri Khan started his legislative career with the 
membership of the Uttar Pradesh Le gislative Assembly in 1974 and 
continued till 1977. He was again elected to that Assembly in 1977 and 1980. 
Shri Khan served as a Cabinet Minist er in the Uttar Pradesh Government, 
holding the portfolios of P.W.D., Haj,  Wakf, Cultural Affairs, Jail, Urban 
Development and Revenue, between 1977 and 1980. Shri Khan represented 
the State of Uttar Pradesh in this House from July. 1992 to July, 1998. He 
was also elected to the Uttar Pradesh Legislative Council in 
1998. 
In the passing away of Shri Mohd. Masud Khan, the country has lost 
a distinguished social worker and a noted political worker. 
I also refer with profound sorrow to the dastardly killing of at least 
27 people and injury to several others, mainly, the poor and the labourers, by 
the terrorists, at Kasim Nagar near Narwal bypass, on the outskirts of Jammu 
City on 13th July, 2002. No words are strong enough to condemn this heinous 
act. I am sure the whole House will join me In condemning this dastardly act 
against humanity, which is contrary to the human, ethos, and which has 
shocked the entire civilized world. I hope the House will join me in offering 
our deep condolences to the bereaved families. 
We deeply mourn the passing away of Shri Basappa Danappa Jatti, 
Shri Chandra Mohan Sinha, Shri Gulsher Ahmed, Shri Sundar Mohun 
Hemrom, Shri Mukesh R. Patel, Shri Jagdambi Prasad Yadav and Shri Mohd. 
Masud Khan, and the dastardly killing of the poor and the labourers at Jammu 
City. 
5 

RAJYA SABHA         [15 July, 2002] 
I request Members to rise in their places and observe silence as a 
mark of respect to the memory of the departed. 
(Hon. Members then stood in silence for one minute.) 
MR. CHAIRMAN: Secretary-General will convey to the members 
of the bereaved families our sense of profound sorrow and deep sympathy. 
As a mark of respect to the memory of Shri Basappa Danappa Jatti, 
former Chairman of Rajya Sabha, and Shri Mukesh R. Patel, a sitting 
Member of this House, the House stands adjourned till 11.00 a.m. on 
Tuesday, the 16th July, 2002.
